card.name: Drug metabolism and enzyme interaction text
card.fires_on: Linking or partial words inside drug-metabolism passages, such as after a drug name, inside CYP or UGT enzyme names, or inside metabolite names. Typical setting is drug interaction sections on statins, CYP enzymes and glucuronides.

modes.label: Linking words after drug names
modes.description: Small words like 'and' or 'the' right after a drug name, before its metabolite or acid form.
modes.example: 3 to 4 fold increases in plasma concentrations of atorvastatin<< and>> atorvastatin lactone were

modes.label: Inside enzyme names
modes.description: Partway through CYP or UGT enzyme names and the long name of uridine glucuronosyltransferase.

modes.label: Inside metabolite names
modes.description: Partway through names of metabolites such as glucuronide conjugates.
modes.example: The acyl-β-glucuron<<ide>> metabolite of clopidogrel is

card.writes: It suppresses chromatography-related tokens like chrom and LC, so it steers the model away from chromatography words in these metabolism passages.
card.plain: It fires in drug-interaction text about liver enzymes and metabolites, and it steers away from chromatography wording.
